computation_or_rationale: Limited assurance on a nonissuer's financial statements = review under SSARS (AR-C 90); AT-C 210 excludes historical FS reviews; GAAS/PCAOB are audits (reasonable assurance).

AU-C 200.25: 'should' = presumptively mandatory; comply unless in rare circumstances a departure is justified and alternative procedures achieve the intent, documented per AU-C 230.13. (c) is closest though it omits 'rare circumstances'.
AU-C 200 premise: management is responsible for preparation and fair presentation of the FS.
Exchange-listed company = issuer; audit under PCAOB standards (SOX 103).
AU-C 200.A: inherent limitations (nature of financial reporting/judgment, nature of procedures/sampling, concealed fraud, timeliness/cost) preclude absolute assurance.
Premise covers management's responsibilities (FS; internal control; access). Auditor does not detect all fraud; reasonable assurance re material misstatement only.

Accepting explanation without corroboration because of past honesty violates professional skepticism (AU-C 200.A: belief management is honest does not permit less than persuasive evidence). Note (d) due professional care is the umbrella that includes skepticism (AS 1000) - (a) is the more specific/best answer.
SOC 1 examinations are performed under SSAEs (AT-C 320) issued by the AICPA ASB.

AICPA: 'may/might/could' describe application/explanatory material; no requirement (auditor must understand the entire text). Under PCAOB Rule 3101 'may' = responsibility to consider; stem does not name the framework.
AU-C 200/240: obtain reasonable assurance that FS as a whole are free of material misstatement whether due to fraud or error.
Single audit under Uniform Guidance requires GAGAS (Yellow Book), which incorporates GAAS for financial audits (plus Uniform Guidance compliance requirements).
Determining materiality is a central application of professional judgment (AU-C 200.A; AU-C 320).

AU-C 230.13: document the justification for the departure and how the alternative procedures achieve the intent of the requirement. Stem's 'better achieves' trigger is loose (departure only when specified procedure would be ineffective in rare circumstances).
Anchoring: relying on initial reference point (prior-year audited amount) without independent expectation.
The GAO (Comptroller General) issues GAGAS.
AU-C 500.11: when evidence from one source is inconsistent with another the auditor determines what modifications/additions to procedures are needed to resolve the matter.
AU-C 700.44 (and A): a nonissuer audit conducted under both GAAS and PCAOB standards may state the audit was conducted in accordance with both.
Inquiry alone is not sufficient appropriate evidence for a material item (AU-C 500); corroboration needed.
AU-C 200.25: 'must' = unconditional requirement.
AU-C 200.A: auditor should consider applicable interpretive publications; if not applied, be prepared to explain how GAAS requirements were complied with.
AU-C 200.A: other auditing publications (textbooks etc.) have no authoritative status but may help understand/apply GAAS.
AICPA Auditing Standards Board issues GAAS (SASs/AU-C) for nonissuers.
AU-C 200.12: obtain reasonable assurance FS free from material misstatement (fraud or error) and report in accordance with findings.
Same as aud-ps-19: AICPA ASB.

AU-C 200.25: 'should' = presumptively mandatory.
AU-C 230.13: document justification and how alternative procedures achieve the intent.
AU-C 700: report may state the audit was conducted under both GAAS and PCAOB standards.
Engagement partner must ensure the team collectively has appropriate competence (SAS 146 / AU-C 220); use auditor's specialist (AU-C 620) or consult.
AU-C 585: assess importance of the omitted procedure to present ability to support the opinion; then apply procedures if needed.
Reasonable assurance = high but not absolute level of assurance (AU-C 200.06).
AU-C 200.14 definition: questioning mind + alertness + critical assessment of evidence; neither assumes dishonesty nor unquestioned honesty.
Nonissuer ERISA plan audits follow GAAS (AU-C 703) issued by the AICPA ASB; DOL sets reporting/independence rules, not auditing standards.
Private company audit: AICPA SASs (AU-C).

AU-C 230.A: retention ordinarily no shorter than five years from the report release date (PCAOB: seven years).
